captures.description: Clean bidirectional TCP+HTTP session: handshake, request, 200 OK, graceful FIN close.
Four SYN retries to port 8443, no SYN/ACK ever returned; connection never establishes.
SYN answered immediately with RST/ACK: connection actively refused.
Same 1400-byte segment sent three times with RTO backoff before it is finally ACKed.
Missing server segment triggers 3 duplicate ACKs and a fast retransmit.
Server segments arrive 1,2,4,3,5 - one segment delivered out of sequence order.
Receiver advertises window 0 for ~1.3 s, sender probes, window finally re-opens.
Sender fills the receiver's entire advertised 8192-byte window and stalls awaiting an ACK.
Established session torn down by a server RST 2 s after the client request, with no response data.
Handshake RTT of 412 ms and data ACK RTT of ~410 ms with no loss.
One NXDOMAIN answer plus a second query retried 3x with no answer at all.
One DNS answer takes 2.45 s; a control query answers in 8 ms.
Four DHCP DISCOVERs with exponential backoff and no OFFER on the wire.
Two MACs claim 192.168.1.77 (duplicate address), followed by a 12-target ARP sweep.
ICMP TTL exceeded, port unreachable, and fragmentation-needed responses.
Two healthy TCP handshakes on 802.1Q VLANs 10 and 20 on the same trunk.
IPv6 TCP handshake followed by a TLS ClientHello with SNI secure.example.net.
TLS ClientHello (SNI broken.example.net) answered with fatal alert 40 handshake_failure.
HTTP/1.1 request answered with 500 after 5.18 s server think time, then a fast 404.
pcapng with two IDBs; the same session captured on both interfaces (SPAN duplication).
Client-side-only capture with 96-byte snaplen: no server frames at all, payload truncated.
